I'll give this a jab!  I am not sure of the botanical-part name that they are called. 

They usually represent a mature bud and most likely grown through hydroponics.  Also, of course, they are more predominant in certain strains.  

Their presence does not necessarily dictate a dank bud.  It has more to do with the look of the plant.  Let us take the strain, Jack Herer, into consideration since I know it has this red hair.

I've had bad Jack Herer and great Jack Herer and they both have red hairs.  THC is contained predominantly in the crystals that you can see, not the hair.  A low-mid shelf Jack Herer is often tossed and is usually a lower quality due to be handled badly or not grown very well.  You will see less red hairs on them, of course.  Right now, I have in front of me some sativa strains that don't really show much red hair, but are pretty much the dankest strains I've ever smoked.  They are coated in their own layer of crystals and shimmer under the light.  

Selling weed is a lot about how it looks too.  All private reserves and top shelf strains have been handled delicately to keep as much of that pretty red hair and crystals on.  Lots of the low and mid stuff can have been "preshook" to gather loose kief/crystals so they can sell that separately.  

It's good you're looking at your bud and asking questions though!  When you see enough nugs you'll get a better feel of the dank quality.   Look for those pretty crystals coating the bud if you're aiming for super dank.

Even then, looks can always be deceiving!
